page_title: Ukelele - Keyboard Layout Editor for macOS

summary.name: Ukelele
summary.one_liner: Ukelele is a free Unicode keyboard layout editor for macOS that lets you create and modify .keylayout files by dragging characters onto a graphical keyboard.
use_cases: Creating a custom keyboard layout for a non-Latin script or language
Assigning special Unicode characters to keys on a Mac
Building dead keys for accented character input
Modifying an existing .keylayout file without editing XML by hand
Mapping multiple-character strings to a single keystroke
summary.what_it_does: Ukelele provides a graphical editor for macOS keyboard layouts, which are stored as XML-based .keylayout files. Users drag and drop characters directly onto keys instead of editing the XML by hand. It supports assigning multiple-character strings to keys and creating dead keys that modify the following keystroke. The page says it integrates with Keyboard Juggler for managing layouts. Installing a layout means copying the .keylayout file to /Library or ~/Library and enabling it under the Input Sources settings in System Preferences.
notable: Drag-and-drop graphical editing of .keylayout XML files
Supports dead keys and multiple-character string output
Written by John Brownie of SIL
caveats: Provided under a freeware license with no warranty and no guarantee of support or future upgrades
Latest version requires macOS 12.0 or later
Layouts made with it are .keylayout files and are not compatible with Keyman, which must be installed separately
